title: E07 — Provision Tier-1 DF/DFHack reference environment (Linux + Classic + disposable forts)
description:
## Deliverable
The reproducible game testbed every bridge WP depends on: Dwarf Fortress Classic + DFHack on the
Tier-1 Linux reference platform, with disposable fortress seeds and a version manifest.

## Scope (platform doctrine: README "Platform and distribution support")
- Install DF Classic (free, official Bay 12 build — 53.16 era) + matching DFHack on a Linux worker
  (trj is the natural host). Record exact version/build identities in a compatibility manifest
  (design/registries/COMPATIBILITY.md tuple).
- Disposable fortress harness: seeded world-gen recipes + save templates so WP-09/WP-10 probes and
  fault campaigns never touch a fort worth keeping; restore-from-seed between runs.
- Headless/CLI operability check: DFHack remote interface reachable; bridge plugin skeleton loads
  (full bridge is WP-08/WP-09 — this bead only guarantees the game side).
- Named-version matrix starter: one DF/DFHack pair fully recorded; matrix growth is WP-09+ scope.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Environment smoke script with structured JSON-line output: versions, DFHack RPC reachability,
  save/restore round-trip, seed determinism (same seed → identical embark).
- Each probe run writes an artifact dir (logs, save hashes, manifest snapshot).

## Acceptance
A documented one-command environment rebuild + smoke pass; WP-09/WP-10 can consume it as a
fixture source. Tier 2/3 (Premium Linux, Windows) and macOS-Wine are explicitly out of scope here.

title: E09 — Evidence export for memory curation: dfmcp artifacts → ee remember batches
description:
## Deliverable
Templates + (later) tooling that turn dfmcp artifacts into `ee remember --batch` input: doctor
bundle findings, obligation outcomes (terminal-predicate proofs), fault-campaign reports,
qualification receipts.

## Scope
- Mapping spec: which artifact fields become memory level/kind (procedural rule vs fact vs
  anti-pattern), and the mandatory provenance block (anchor epoch/sequence/state_hash, evidence
  bundle digest, artifact path).
- Batch templates for the laboratory slice today (lab transcript events + session outcomes);
  production evidence bundles arrive with WP-11/WP-12 durable custody.
- Promotion discipline follows ee's "evidence before promotion": curated, provenance-carrying
  entries only; no automatic ingestion of raw logs.
- Cap: no automatic ingestion into canonical dfmcp state — one-way flow dfmcp → ee.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Template round-trip tests: artifact → batch → ee store → `ee search --explain` retrieval with
  provenance fields asserted present.
- Negative: entries without provenance rejected by template lint.

title: Replace plan.rs too_many_arguments allow with a sealed-plan builder
description:
## Task
`PreparedPlan::from_parts` (crates/dfmcp-intent/src/plan.rs) currently carries
`#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` (9-arg constructor mirroring the frozen plan shape).

## Deliverable
A `PreparedPlanBuilder` (or from(Intent, PreparedParts) struct) that groups the arguments
semantically (identity: intent_id; context: anchor+summary+terminal; body: steps+max_risk+
required_capabilities; policy: requires_checkpoint+expires_at_tick) so the allow attribute can be
deleted. Digest derivation MUST be byte-identical to today (TEST-009 plan sealing still passes;
golden plan digests unchanged).

## Acceptance
allow attribute removed; existing plan tests + digest vectors green.

## Background
Flagged during the 2026-08-29 clippy pass (floating-nightly lint drift batch). Do NOT change the
sealed-field set — every covered-field mutation must still invalidate preparation.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Digest-identity tests: builder-produced plans byte-identical to from_parts plans (golden
  digests); full plan test suite green unchanged.

title: WP-00 — Contract repository: registries, schemas, and pure scaffold
description:
## Deliverable
Plan, design registries, JSON schemas, protobuf contract, and a pure safe-Rust scaffold that
freezes vocabulary before any implementation claims.

## Scope (already satisfied — this bead is closed for the record)
- README/ARCHITECTURE/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS/MCP_SURFACE + docs/* design corpus.
- `design/registries/` (INVARIANTS INV-001..050, ACTIONS, CAPABILITIES, EFFECTS, ERRORS,
  DETERMINISM, SCHEMAS, TESTS, COMPATIBILITY, WORK_PACKAGES).
- `schemas/dfmcp.schema.json` (frozen 11-tool surface) + per-tool entry schemas; `proto/dfmcp.proto`
  (11-bridge-RPC contract, design-only).
- `architecture/` machine registries: dependency_allowlist.toml, franken_imports.json,
  publication_primitives.json, graph_algorithms.json.
- `scripts/validate_repo.py` (contract validator), `scripts/check_dependency_policy.py`,
  `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/qualify_local.sh` (machine-readable qualification receipts).

## Acceptance gate
`repository validator; no false implementation claims` — currently enforced as 423 checks across
120+ files, plus the dependency-policy gate. Both green (see IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md).

## Background
Everything downstream compiles against frozen vocabulary. Changing registries requires an ADR in
the same commit as the registry update (CONTRIBUTING.md). The validator hard-fails on
overclaiming: IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md must keep denying a production MCP server and live DFHack.
close_reason: Contract repository complete and verified: registries, schemas, proto contract, pure scaffold, validators (423 checks green). See IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md Phase 0A/0B record.

title: WP-02 — World graph: entity/edge/fact/spatial model integrity
description:
## Deliverable
Bring `crates/dfmcp-world` model layer to the WP-02 gate: integrity and ABA tests.

## Current state
Typed property graph (EntityRecord/EdgeRecord with Fact provenance: value, observed tick, source
digest, schema version), MapChunk with TerrainRun RLE + bitplanes, WorldEvent journal,
WorldSnapshot with hash validation, canonical big-endian encoding helpers, normalized predicates,
hash-anchored StateDelta build/apply with stale-anchor rejection.

## Remaining work to gate
- Integrity invariants as tests: edge endpoints exist, revisions monotone, aggregates consistent
  (TEST-005); deletion/ID-reuse/generation-mismatch/stale-reference behavior (TEST-002).
- Fact presence algebra: unknown/omitted/unsupported/null/stale distinction (TEST-003;
  docs/WORLD_MODEL.md notes presence algebra is the next schema item).
- Chunk canonical hashing: bitplane + RLE golden vectors; sparse-overlay equivalence tests.

## Acceptance gate
`integrity and ABA tests` green in verify.sh; no false-positive freshness.

## Background
The canonical model is deliberately distinct from raw DFHack structures, MCP presentation JSON,
search indexes, and agent memory (README "Canonical world model"). Entities are graph nodes; the
map is chunks, never millions of nodes. ABA reuse is prevented by entity generation numbers;
revision orders updates within a generation (docs/WORLD_STATE_MVCC.md).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Unit: integrity invariant checks per operation (endpoint existence, revision monotonicity).
- Property: random graph mutations → invariants hold; ABA: delete+reuse attempts must trip
  generation checks with the offending IDs logged.
- Golden: chunk RLE/bitplane hash vectors; sparse-overlay vs dense equivalence with per-chunk
  diff logs on mismatch.
- Negative evidence: stale-reference rejections recorded with anchors; artifacts under
  `crates/dfmcp-world/tests/artifacts/`.

title: WP-05 — Intent compiler: normalized actions, constraints, sealed plans
description:
## Deliverable
Harden `crates/dfmcp-intent` to the WP-05 gate: mutation-digest and risk tests.

## Current state
10 semantic Action variants (Pause, DesignateDig, Build, SetLabor, CreateWorkOrder,
ConfigureStockpile, AssignSquad, SetBurrowMembership, SetStandingOrder, Extension) with
normalization/encoding; Constraint enum; ObligationSpec; RequestedAction with pre/postconditions,
compensation, obligation, depends_on; Intent; PreparedPlan validation pipeline (digest-derived
IDs, dependency DAG validation, postcondition checks); StaticPlanner prepare() with anchor
freshness, capability authorization, budget/limit enforcement.

## Remaining work to gate
- Normalization property: equivalent inputs → equal digest; malformed input rejection (TEST-007).
- Plan sealing: every covered-field mutation invalidates preparation (TEST-009) — plan id and
  digest are derived from sealed content (current digest-derived IDs already enforce this; prove it).
- Risk/capability lattice tests: no amplification, monotonicity (TEST-008).
- Predicted semantic diff + witnessed read/write sets (currently design-only:
  IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md intent row) — positive, negative, range, aggregate, spatial, epoch
  witnesses per docs/WORLD_STATE_MVCC.md.
- Recipe planner for registered action families (mine/channel/stairs patterns etc.,
  design/registries/ACTIONS.md).

## Acceptance gate
`mutation-digest and risk tests` green.

## Background
Semantic intents compile into immutable, capability-checked action DAGs (README). A plan is sealed
over intent, source state hash, steps, dependencies, pre/postconditions, compensation, obligations,
risk, capabilities, expiry — commit requires exact plan ID + digest + prepare receipt + expected
anchor; duplicates return the prior receipt (ADR-006/ADR-010). plan.rs from_parts carries
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] — replace with a builder API when touching this file (be
dfmcp-plan-builder-api).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Digest property tests: semantically-equivalent intent rewrites → identical digest; each
  covered-field mutation of a sealed plan → prepared-plan invalidation (table-driven, every field).
- Malformed-input rejection suite: per-field invalid cases with expected ErrorCode.
- Risk lattice: grant×action pairs asserted against the capability matrix.
- Witness tests (once witnessed sets land): positive/negative/range/aggregate/spatial witness
  capture round-trips; logs record witness kinds per step.

title: WP-09 — DFHack read bridge: canonical fortress snapshots/deltas
description:
## Deliverable
First live read path: read-only bridge handshake + one coherently published observation capsule.
This is IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md's named "next executable milestone".

## Scope
- DFHack-side bridge plugin/service (out-of-process, versioned; Lua/remote-interface bridge per
  docs/DFHACK_BRIDGE.md) speaking WP-08's framed protocol.
- Compatibility probe + manifests (DF version/build, DFHack version/commit, bridge protocol+schema
  digest — design/registries/COMPATIBILITY.md tuple).
- Canonical fortress identity, observation epoch, game tick, pause state, bounded unit summary
  with provenance; state anchor; immutable capsule digest.
- doctor report + replayable evidence bundle; golden fixtures per supported pair.

## Acceptance gate
`compatibility fixtures and live smoke` — against disposable forts only (TESTS.md TEST-019;
QUALIFICATION Q4). Read-only: no mutation admission in this WP.

## Platform note (see README "Platform and distribution support")
Tier-1 reference: Linux + free Dwarf Fortress Classic + DFHack (53.16 era). Premium Linux tier 2;
Windows tier 3; macOS only via Wine, best effort — development happens on Linux workers (trj).

## Background
This is implementation-program gate 2 ("authoritative read path"). Live control is explicitly NOT
implemented (IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md); this WP is where that begins, gated on probes.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Compatibility fixtures: golden snapshot/delta pairs per supported DF/DFHack tuple, stored with
  the environment manifest from the Tier-1 game env bead.
- Live smoke: scripted handshake → capsule publication → doctor report, JSON-line logs at every
  stage (manifests, anchor, capsule digest, unit summary bounds).
- Negative: malformed/oversized bridge frames, disconnect/restart mid-read — each logged with
  the recovery path taken. Disposable forts only; save hashes recorded per run.

title: WP-11 — Durable ledger: FrankenSQLite-backed WAL/state
description:
## Deliverable
FrankenSQLite-backed canonical ledger: MVCC world state, effect journal, recovery.

## Current state
Design only (IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md persistence row; docs/WORLD_STATE_MVCC.md). FrankenSQLite
(fsqlite) is the owned sibling providing multi-version semantic snapshots, positive/negative SSI
witnesses, hierarchical no-false-negative conflict refinement, brief commit combining,
deterministic intent replay, stable-key structural merge, trace-normal-form + post-state
certificates (README Franken stack table; architecture/franken_imports.json).

## Remaining work to gate
- Ledger schema for: canonical capsule stream, plans, receipts, effect journal, leases, evidence.
- Crash-point matrix (TEST-016): kill at every durable transition, recover honestly;
  indeterminate effects stay indeterminate until reconciled.
- Witness validation integration with WP-06 coordinator (negative-read phantom protection).

## Acceptance gate
`crash-point matrix` green.

## Background
The canonical world is multi-version; never replaced by one mutable current snapshot (project
AGENTS.md state rules). Derived state can always be discarded and rebuilt from capsules.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Crash-point matrix: enumerate every durable transition; kill (SIGKILL) at each; restart and
  assert honest recovery state — per-point recovery transcripts logged (TEST-016).
- Witness integration: negative-read phantom insertion attempts must be caught — repro scripts
  retained.
- Receipts: verify.sh receipt + matrix artifact dir committed as evidence inputs.

title: WP-13 gate 2 — session-scoped capability negotiation
description:
## Task
Replace the process-global laboratory session (LabState in crates/dfmcp-mcp/src/server.rs) with
per-session state and capability grants negotiated in fortress_open_session.

## Current state
Slice-1 keeps ONE process-local session: `static LAB: LazyLock<Mutex<LabState>>` with grants baked
into context_for (observe/query/plan/control_clock/checkpoint/restore at fixed risk tiers).
Documented in server.rs module docs + FASTMCP_INTEGRATION.md gate 2.

## Deliverables
- Per-connection session identity: fastmcp session state (SessionState map) or owned task store
  holds the LabSession; parallel clients get isolated fortresses (or correctly scoped shared
  ones) with no cross-talk.
- fortress.open_session arguments negotiate: capability set, risk ceilings, work budgets,
  fortress selector. Grants come from dfmcp-core CapabilityGrant — never from transport identity
  (FASTMCP_INTEGRATION.md §6).
- Lease groundwork hooks for WP-15 (lease ids in grants).
- Multi-client tests: two concurrent stdio sessions; isolation + independent anchors.

## Acceptance
WP-13 gate 2 closed: multi-client safe; grants negotiated per session; no process-global
authority. Token budgets still enforced server-side.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Two concurrent stdio sessions: isolated anchors, isolated lab state, independent plan/commit
  flows; cross-talk attempt logs.
- Grant negotiation: capability subset requests honored/rejected per dfmcp-core scope rules;
  transport identity never grants authority (negative test).

title: WP-13 — MCP server: 11-tool waist over the pinned fastmcp_rust plane
description:
## Deliverable
The 11-tool fortress.* narrow waist over the owned fastmcp_rust sibling (ADR-013), modern-only
MCP 2026-07-28. Managed in gates:

- Gate 1 (DONE — this bead intentionally stays OPEN as the program anchor; its WP-table
blockers WP03/04/06/07 keep it open): stdio laboratory slice — all 11 tools over MemoryAdapter
  in crates/dfmcp-mcp; `dwarf-fortress-mcp serve`; digest-matched plan commit; era negotiation
  live on the wire. MCP tool names render logical dots as underscores.
- Gate 2 (bead dfmcp-wp13-gate2-session-authority): session-scoped capability negotiation.
- Gate 3 (bead dfmcp-wp13-gate3-tasks-binding): MCP Tasks backed by the obligation engine via
  ServerBuilder::final_tasks.
- Gate 4 = WP-14 (Streamable HTTP).

## Current state (gate 1, verified 2026-08-29)
Full verify.sh ladder green on Linux nightly 1.100.0 (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, rustdoc,
contract checks). Transport pinned: fastmcp_rust 6481d49 (upstream fixes #59/#60). Modern-only
profile machine-enforced (scripts/check_dependency_policy.py + validate_repo.py).

## Acceptance gate (overall)
`MCP 2026-07-28 conformance and token budgets` (with WP-21).

## Background
Wire names render logical dots as underscores (registry names keep dots). The transport adds no
authority; no fastmcp type crosses the intent/world/adapter seams (docs/FASTMCP_INTEGRATION.md).
Initialization-based MCP is disabled in this builder profile — modern sessions negotiate via
server/discover and per-request _meta era markers; exact client shapes are validated under WP-21.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Gate-1 evidence (recorded): full verify.sh ladder green on Linux nightly 1.100.0 at pin
  6481d49 — fmt, clippy -D warnings, workspace tests (incl. dfmcp-mcp seed-snapshot tests),
  warning-free rustdoc, contract checks (contract/doctor/demo).
- Wire-level: live stdio JSON-RPC smoke — framing, era negotiation, per-request modern markers
  (full modern client session goldens tracked in dfmcp-wp13-modern-handshake-golden).
- Known slice-1 simplification, fixed in this revision: duplicate commit with the same digest now
  replays the prior receipt verbatim (ADR-006 idempotency) instead of erroring; covered by the
  gate-2 test pass.
- Gate 2/3 work carries its own test sections (see session-authority and tasks-binding beads).

title: Validate modern stdio session shapes and lock golden tests
description:
## Task
Pin down the exact modern-era stdio session flow observed during integration and freeze it as
golden tests (feeds WP-21/TEST-023).

## Observed behavior (2026-08-29, raw JSON-RPC over stdio vs `dwarf-fortress-mcp serve`)
- Newline-delimited JSON-RPC; server live and era-aware; era refusal carries
  `supported: ["2026-07-28","2024-11-05"]`.
- Opening frame rules (from fastmcp_rust StdioEraClassifier): an initialize carrying BOTH
  protocolVersion and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` is rejected
  (MixedEraMarkers); a bare initialize under Auto selects the legacy era (our no-legacy build
  then refuses it as cross-era); initialization-based MCP is disabled in this builder profile —
  modern sessions use `server/discover` instead of initialize.
- Per-request modern metadata `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"] = "2026-07-28"`
  is required once modern is selected; first frame must therefore be a modern-tagged request
  (e.g. tools/list or server/discover), not initialize.
- Open questions to nail down: valid server/discover params shape; valid modern tools/list params
  (bare `{"_meta": ...}` was rejected as invalid params); notification rules after selection.

## Deliverables
- Golden request/response transcripts as test fixtures driving the real stdio server.
- A documented "modern client quickstart" snippet in docs/FASTMCP_INTEGRATION.md.
- Feed any spec-conformance doubts into upstream issues per docs/DOGFOODING_FASTMCP.md.

## Acceptance
A scripted client completes discover → tools/list → tools/call(fortress_open_session →
fortress_plan → fortress_commit) against `serve` in CI-runnable form (trj or local post-rustup-repair).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Scripted client (JSON-lines over stdio) completing discover → tools/list →
  open_session → plan → commit, with full request/response transcripts checked in as fixtures.
- Negative fixtures: mixed-initialize rejection, bare-initialize cross-era refusal — exact error
  codes/messages asserted so upstream behavior changes are caught on pin bumps.

title: WP-14 — HTTP/session mode: Streamable HTTP, auth, reconnect
description:
## Deliverable
Streamable HTTP transport for the same 11-tool surface (fastmcp_rust HTTP transport, still
modern-only, localhost-first), plus session durability.

## Scope
- Enable the facade HTTP path behind the same dfmcp-mcp tools (no semantic changes).
- Duplicate/disconnect/load tests (WP-14 gate): duplicate submission, reconnect, session resume,
  idempotency across reconnects (TESTS.md families; ROADMAP Phase 4).
- Transport-boundary admission design before any non-localhost bind (FASTMCP_INTEGRATION.md §6;
  no auth features are enabled in the admitted profile).
- Output budgets enforced server-side; never truncate mid-object (MCP_SURFACE.md).

## Acceptance gate
`duplicate/disconnect/load tests` green; GATE-040 contribution.

## Dependencies
WP-13 gates 2-3 (session-scoped authority must exist before multi-client HTTP).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Duplicate submission, mid-stream disconnect, reconnect+resume, and load soak (concurrent
  sessions) — per-connection JSON-line logs, session ids, resume tokens.
- Cross-transport semantics: identical tool results via stdio and HTTP for the same anchor
  (differential log on drift).
- Admission: non-localhost bind attempts rejected until the transport-boundary admission design
  lands (negative test).

title: WP-15 — Leases/delegation: scoped multi-agent coordination
description:
## Deliverable
Multi-agent safe concurrency: leases fence who may act; MVCC witnesses prove facts still hold.

## Scope (design source: docs/WORLD_STATE_MVCC.md, README multi-agent operation)
- Lease objects: owners, scopes (entity generations, map cuboids, resource classes, config
  domains, plan/obligation ownership, simulation clock), epochs, expiries, fencing tokens, budgets.
- Witness refinement under a value-of-information budget; exhaustion → conservative replan, never
  guessed safety. Negative/aggregate witnesses so later inserts cannot become invisible phantoms.
- Disjoint plans commit concurrently; overlapping plans: deterministic intent replay → stable-key
  structural merge → reject+replan; accepted merges carry canonical certificates (proof-carrying
  merge).
- Delegated capabilities + branch-per-agent isolation (ROADMAP Phase 10; GATE-100).

## Acceptance gate
`DPOR conflict/fencing tests` (TEST-018: stale fences, overlap, commutative actions, starvation).

## Background
Cooperation without a global mutex and without optimistic hand-waving (README). Industrial
protocol: lease theft and multi-agent conflicts are a core threat class (SECURITY.md).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- DPOR-style schedule enumeration over overlapping plan pairs: assert either disjoint success or
  documented merge/rejection with certificates — schedules and outcomes logged (TEST-018).
- Fencing: stale-fence takeover attempts rejected; fencing-token lineage logged.
- Starvation: weighted fairness assertions under contention.
- Merge certificates: canonical proof validated byte-exact on every accepted merge.

title: WP-17 — FrankenMarkdown knowledge: lossless guides/runbooks/policies
description:
## Deliverable
Imported docs/knowledge plane: exact-span provenance, bounded parsing, taint tracking.

## Scope
- franken_markdown-based knowledge resources (df://knowledge/{document}/{span} — MCP_SURFACE.md).
- Exact bytes, spans, transformation lineage, taint (docs/FRANKEN_INTEGRATION.md FrankenMarkdown
  section). In-game text and imported docs are DATA: they cannot grant capabilities or become
  commands (project AGENTS.md; SECURITY.md prompt-injection threat class).
- Byte-span and taint tests (TEST-020 prompt/taint security family).
- Lossless guides/runbooks/policies with bounded non-recursive parsing.

## Acceptance gate
`byte-span and taint tests` green; hostile content corpus handled fail-closed.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Byte-span round-trip: extracted spans reassemble to source bytes exactly (hash-checked).
- Taint corpus: hostile docs (injection payloads, fake capability grants) → parsed as data only,
  assertions that no capability/authority edge is created; corpus retained with per-doc verdicts.
- Bounds: non-recursive parse depth/nesting limit tests with rejection logs.

title: E08 — ee campaign workflow: per-fortress memory workspace validated end to end
description:
## Deliverable
Validate and document the Eidetic Engine (`ee`) campaign workflow for fortress stewardship
(doctrine: docs/EIDETIC_MEMORY.md; COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN Part XXIII).

## Scope
- Per-fortress `--workspace` scoping conventions (one ee workspace per campaign; naming; backup
  story — ee workspaces are agent state, not project state).
- End-to-end walkthrough on the laboratory slice: session start (`ee resume`, `ee pack --read-only`),
  anchor-referenced `ee remember` entries citing lab transcript events + state hashes, retrieval
  via `ee search --explain` / `ee why`.
- Revivable lessons: `--revive-when path_exists:` mapped to fortress preconditions (e.g., revive
  "build the magma-safe bridge" when a reserve exists).
- `ee preflight check` advisory lookups for risky operations — documented as advisory-only;
  authority remains capabilities + plan sealing.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Scripted walkthrough transcript checked into docs (commands + outputs with provenance fields).
- Negative doctrine test in review checklist: any memory cited AS state fails review.

## Background
Agents that forget re-dig the same aquifer. Memory is speculative by constitution (README
canonical-model note; Part XXIII): advisory context with provenance pointers, never authority.

title: E10 — Multi-agent shared campaign memory policy (ee team), gated on WP-15
description:
## Deliverable
Policy for SHARED campaign memory across multiple agents operating one fortress: what may be
shared, what stays per-agent, and how leases govern memory-derived claims.

## Scope
- `ee team` adoption only after WP-15 leases/delegation land: a shared memory entry is still
  advisory; taking action on it requires that agent's own authority and fresh observations.
- Conflict policy: two agents record contradictory lessons → provenance + recency rules, then
  human/`ee curate` resolution; never silent overwrite (ee: no silent memory mutation).
- Per-agent private memory conventions (hedged strategies, counterfactual branch notes —
  branch-per-agent isolation in WP-15).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Policy walkthrough on a two-agent scenario with lease-scoped actions; contradiction-resolution
  transcript retained.
- Dependency honesty: blocked until WP-15 (multi-agent authority) is real.

## Background
Branch-per-agent isolation and delegated capabilities (WP-15) define what "shared" can mean;
memory without authority remains advisory (Part XXIII).

title: Repair Mac rustup nightly toolchain (local qualification unblocked)
description:
## Problem
rustup channel sync on this Mac fails: component updates roll back with hundreds of
`os error 66` (Directory not empty) rename errors against
`~/.rustup/toolchains/nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin`. Consequence: `cargo` on the Mac cannot run
verify.sh locally; all Rust gates currently run on the trj Linux worker via rch.

## Fix (requires explicit user approval — deletion-adjacent)
Standard repair: `rustup toolchain uninstall nightly` then reinstall with the components required
by rust-toolchain.toml (clippy, rustfmt, rust-src, llvm-tools-preview — the repo validator
enforces their presence). Optionally pin rust-toolchain.toml to a dated nightly IF the project
chooses to amend the "must track latest nightly" validator rule (currently floating by design).

## Acceptance
`cargo --version && cargo clippy --version` succeed on the Mac; `DFMCP_ALLOW_MISSING_RUST unset
./scripts/verify.sh` runs the Rust gates locally.

## Background
Discovered 2026-08-29 during the fastmcp adoption publish; static-only receipts are
non-release-admissible by design, so local capability matters for Q1 evidence diversity
(docs/LOCAL_QUALIFICATION_AND_RELEASE.md).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Post-repair acceptance: `cargo --version`, `cargo clippy --version`, and a full local
  `./scripts/verify.sh` (Rust gates NOT skipped) with the receipt committed as evidence.

title: Bump fastmcp_rust pin to v0.8.0 preflight (12d3469+) with conformance note
description:
## Task
Advance `[mcp_transport].pin` + workspace Cargo.toml rev from 6481d49 to the v0.8.0 preflight
head (12d3469 or later green rev), per docs/DOGFOODING_FASTMCP.md "Taking fixes upstream → pin
bumps".

## Steps
1. Sync the pin in architecture/dependency_allowlist.toml + root Cargo.toml.
2. Regenerate Cargo.lock (note: rch remote runs do NOT write back Cargo.lock — regenerate locally
   after the Mac rustup repair (dfmcp-env-mac-rustup-repair), or hand-apply the rev/version diff
   and validate with `cargo check --locked` on trj, which fails loudly on drift).
3. Re-run verify.sh on trj (or locally post-E01) — v0.8.0 restructured sse.rs (legacy SSE code
   removed upstream) and included 3a82c30 non-legacy warning fixes; expect clippy surface changes.
4. Append the pin-history row + conformance note; run WP-21 conformance suite on the new pin.

## Acceptance
New pin green end to end; ledger row appended; no unbundled changes in the bump commit.

## Background
6481d49 remains the verified-green pin; v0.8.0 restructured sse.rs (legacy SSE removed upstream)
and added non-legacy warning fixes (3a82c30). Pins move only forward within a cycle; rollbacks
need a note explaining the forcing regression.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Both transport profiles compile on the new pin (`-p fastmcp-transport` default + no-default).
- Full verify.sh on trj (or locally post-rustup-repair) with receipt; conformance note appended
  to docs/DOGFOODING_FASTMCP.md in the same commit as the bump.

title: WP-01 — Canonical primitives: IDs, digests, anchors, authority, budgets
description:
## Deliverable
Harden `crates/dfmcp-core` into the WP-01 gate: property-tested canonical primitives.

## Current state
dfmcp-core has: SHA-256 digest (in-tree, known-vector tests), 13 typed ID wrappers (u128/u64 via
macro), StateAnchor + ObservationCursor, RiskTier, 18 Capabilities + CapabilityGrant/Scope
authorization logic, WorkBudget, OperationContext, 26 typed ErrorCodes (DfmcpError with retry
semantics), explicit outcomes.

## Remaining work to gate
- Property tests (proptest-style) for digest insertion-order/platform independence and ID/ABA
  generation semantics (TEST-001, TEST-002 in design/registries/TESTS.md).
- Canonical vectors: golden digest vectors for anchored encodings (framing: big-endian, ordered).
- Capability lattice property: no authority amplification; risk monotonicity (TEST-008).
- Bounded-budget semantics: WorkBudget exhaustion behavior tests.

## Acceptance gate
`property tests and canonical vectors` pass in `scripts/verify.sh` on latest nightly.

## Tests to include
Unit + property tests inside dfmcp-core; golden vectors as fixture files with detailed diff
logging. Negative evidence record per TESTS.md preamble (fault hypotheses, seeds, artifacts).

## Background
INV-001..INV-050 (design/registries/INVARIANTS.md, normative source Part III of
COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN) each require two independent enforcement mechanisms eventually; this WP
supplies the first mechanism for the identity/anchor layer. Hash = SHA-256 over explicit framed
ordered bytes (ADR-003); production bounded schema encoding is a follow-up, not a gate blocker.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Unit: per-module in dfmcp-core (`cargo test -p dfmcp-core`), including known-answer SHA-256
  vectors and ID generation edge cases (NIL, max u128, generation wrap).
- Property: digest order/platform independence; scope-amplification impossibility checks
  (random grant pairs, assert rejection) — seeds logged, failures reproduce by seed.
- Golden vectors: `crates/dfmcp-core/tests/vectors/` with a generator + verifier pair; verifier
  diffs byte-by-byte with offset logging on mismatch.
- Evidence: negative-evidence record per TESTS.md preamble (hypotheses, seeds, artifact paths);
  gate runs append to the verify.sh receipt.

title: WP-03 — Delta algebra: snapshots, deltas, continuations, events
description:
## Deliverable
Complete `dfmcp-world` delta algebra to the WP-03 gate: full→delta equivalence corpus.

## Current state
StateDelta with canonical hash anchoring, build_delta/apply_delta, exact-basis requirement,
stale-anchor rejection; observation modes sketched (README "Agent-efficient observation": anchors,
interest sets, semantic deltas, token-budgeted projections, attention ranking).

## Remaining work to gate
- Equivalence corpus: for a battery of seeded world mutations, apply(build_delta(a,b)) == b,
  byte-identical state_hash (TEST-004).
- Gap/fork/duplicate/continuation rejection tests: delta across a cursor gap must fail closed;
  duplicate application must be idempotent-rejected; continuation tokens are opaque and
  anchor-bound (INV set + docs/WORLD_STATE_MVCC.md).
- Event journal ordering + evidence references in deltas.
- Entity-generation ABA via deltas: replay cannot resurrect a dead generation.

## Acceptance gate
`full→delta equivalence corpus` green; rejection paths covered with negative evidence.

## Background
Deltas are the only freshness mechanism agents get — cursor+hash continuity (ADR-004) exists
because sequence numbers alone cannot detect divergent state. Restore/ambiguous restart creates a
new observation epoch and requires full snapshot (MCP_SURFACE.md error behavior).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Equivalence corpus: seeded mutation battery (target ≥1000 scenarios) —
  `apply(build_delta(a,b)) == b` asserted byte-identical; corpus index + per-scenario pass/fail
  JSON-lines log.
- Rejection suite: cursor gap, fork, duplicate, stale-hash — each with the exact ErrorCode
  asserted and the rejected delta retained as an artifact.
- Continuation: opaque-token round-trip across observation boundaries; logs include anchor
  (epoch, sequence) at every step.

title: WP-04 — DfQL core: typed bounded query planner/evaluator
description:
## Deliverable
Implement the DfQL query engine in `dfmcp-world`/`dfmcp-intent` to the WP-04 gate.

## Current state
Predicate enum (All/Any/Not/FieldCompare/EntityExists/Paused) with normalization, CompareOp,
WorldQuery/QueryResult execution, deterministic ordering; QueryOrder including tie-breaks
(label asc + id asc; revision desc + id asc). The dfmcp-mcp fortress_query tool exposes only
mode="summary" and returns a stable "full DfQL is WP-04" message for other modes.

## Remaining work to gate
- Truth-table tests for every Predicate/CompareOp combination (TEST-006).
- Deterministic ordering guarantees: equal inputs → equal output order, across platforms.
- Budget enforcement: entity/byte/token limits with continuation instead of truncation
  (MCP_SURFACE.md output shaping: never truncate mid-object).
- Statically costed query plans (plan rejection over budget before execution).
- Index scaffolding for entity-kind/field lookups (derived, rebuildable, never authoritative).

## Acceptance gate
`truth-table and budget tests` green; dfmcp-mcp fortress_query upgrades from summary-mode to
bounded DfQL execution behind the same tool name.

## Background
Queries run at a concrete anchor with deterministic result ordering (MCP_SURFACE.md); the
attention layer (WP-16) consumes DfQL results. Query economics: common summaries target hundreds
of tokens, not megabytes (README token-budgeted projections).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Truth tables: generated exhaustive tables for Predicate × CompareOp over typed fixtures,
  checked into `crates/dfmcp-world/tests/truthtables/` with a regenerate/verify pair.
- Determinism: same query on same anchor across runs/platforms → identical row order (diff logged
  on drift).
- Budgets: entity/byte/token limit tests with per-limit breach logs and continuation-token
  assertions (never mid-object truncation).
- Plan costing: static cost rejection tests with the cost trace logged.

title: WP-06 — Action coordinator: prepare/commit/idempotency/postconditions
description:
## Deliverable
Promote the prepare/revalidate/commit/observe/prove coordinator to the WP-06 gate.

## Current state
The coordinator flow exists across dfmcp-intent (planner), dfmcp-adapter (GameAdapter trait:
prepare/commit/poll_action/request_cancel/finalize_cancel/checkpoint/restore with receipts), and
dfmcp-lab (MemoryAdapter: commit-time reauthorization, dependency-ordered dispatch, postcondition
checks, CommitState machine incl. AppliedAwaitingVerification/Verified/Failed, idempotent
commits, transcript). dfmcp-mcp fortress_commit exercises digest-matched prepare→commit.

## Remaining work to gate
- Exhaustive state-machine tests: every legal/illegal transition of the mutation state set
  (prepared, committing, applied_awaiting_verification, verified, compensation_pending,
  compensated, cancel_requested, cancelled, failed, indeterminate — MCP_SURFACE.md) (TEST-011).
- Idempotency: duplicate same-content commit returns prior receipt; conflicting content rejected
  (TEST-010).
- Effect journal identity + durable dispatch-attempt records (design: docs/ATP_STATE_AND_EVIDENCE_PLANE.md;
  durable storage is WP-11).
- Indeterminate handling: timeout → indeterminate, blocks blind retry (ADR-008).

## Acceptance gate
`exhaustive state-machine tests` green.

## Background
No transport acknowledgment is success; proof comes from later normalized observations satisfying
registered semantic predicates (README central distinction). Compensation is a separately
authorized new action, never rollback (ADR-009).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- State-machine exhaustiveness: generate the full transition table from the CommitState machine
  definition and test every (state, operation) pair — legal paths and expected-rejection paths —
  with a counterexample log on drift.
- Idempotency: duplicate commit replays prior receipt byte-identical (receipt diff logged);
  conflicting-content rejection asserted.
- Indeterminate: forced-timeout path asserts blind retry is refused with
  reconciliation_required retry class.
- Artifacts: per-run receipt journal excerpts retained under test artifacts.

title: WP-07 — Obligation runtime: temporal completion and cancellation drain
description:
## Deliverable
Build the bounded-obligation runtime to the WP-07 gate.

## Current state
ObligationSpec in dfmcp-intent (terminal/failure predicates, deadline_tick, poll_interval_ticks,
stable_for_observations — validated canonical); MemoryAdapter dispatch_step evaluates
failure/deadline/terminal+stability with stable_observations accounting; poll_action + request/
finalize cancellation with CancelMode (StopFutureSteps, CompensateReversible,
EmergencyPauseAndDrain); dfmcp-mcp fortress_wait/fortress_cancel exercise it.

## Remaining work to gate
- Virtual-time/model tests: completion, blocked, timeout, failure, cancellation, stable
  observations (TEST-012) under a deterministic virtual clock.
- Quantitative cancellation drain with progress certificates (docs/WORLD_STATE_MVCC.md +
  ARCHITECTURE.md: cancellation is request/drain/reconcile/finalize; long drains produce progress
  certificates) — needs asupersync Cx regions (coordinate with WP-18).
- Obligation store as the authoritative backing for MCP Tasks (paired with WP-13 gate 3).
- Failure predicates, compensation policy fields, indeterminate reconciliation paths.

## Acceptance gate
`virtual-time/model tests` green.

## Background
Temporal work is a bounded obligation with semantic terminal predicate, optional failure
predicate, game-tick deadline, polling cadence, stability requirement, evidence references, and
cancellation policy (ADR-007). Cancellation never deletes records (MCP_SURFACE.md).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Virtual-clock model tests: scripted tick timelines covering completion, blocked, timeout,
  failure-predicate trigger, stability-window accounting (stable_for_observations boundary at
  exactly N-1/N), with full tick-by-tick traces in logs.
- Cancellation: request at every await/poll boundary; drain progress certificates asserted;
  compensate path requires authorization (unauthorized-compensation rejection test).
- Determinism: identical virtual schedules → identical transcripts (diff on drift).

title: WP-08 — Bridge protocol: protobuf handshake/read/mutate contracts
description:
## Deliverable
Realize `proto/dfmcp.proto` into the bounded bridge codec with the WP-08 gate.

## Current state
proto/dfmcp.proto (proto3, ~813 lines): DfmcpBridge service with 11 RPCs (Handshake, Health,
ProbeCompatibility, ReadSnapshot, ReadDelta, PrepareMutation, CommitMutation, LookupOperation,
CancelOperation, CreateCheckpoint, RestoreCheckpoint); Digest (32-byte), ObservationCursor,
StateAnchor, ReadGroup enum (13 groups), InterestSet, WorldFrame, StateDelta with DeltaOperation
oneof, receipts, BridgeError. DESIGN-ONLY — no codec exists.

## Remaining work to gate
- Minimal Rust codec (closed-universe compliant: hand-written or owned codec; prost is prohibited
  in this project's own code — see DEPENDENCY_POLICY.md §3) for the exact supported schema.
- Decoder fuzz: lengths, nesting, variants, truncation, corruption (TEST-014) + golden vectors.
- BridgeError taxonomy mapped to dfmcp-core ErrorCodes with retry classes.
- Versioned frame envelope + manifest exchange (bridge/DF/DFHack manifests, COMPATIBILITY registry).

## Acceptance gate
`decoder fuzz and golden vectors` green.

## Background
The bridge is an out-of-process, bounded, versioned loopback (ARCHITECTURE.md trust boundaries);
the Rust trust domain never links C/C++ (ADR-001). Arbitrary Lua/shell/DFHack commands are never
exposed (OPERATIONS + project AGENTS.md).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Codec round-trip property tests over generated frames (all 11 RPCs, all ReadGroups).
- Fuzz harness (deterministic seeds, closed-universe: hand-rolled generator, no external fuzz
  runtime in the trust domain): truncation at every byte offset class, nested-depth overflow,
  unknown variants/fields preserved-not-crashed — artifacts (failing frames) retained with seed
  logs.
- Golden vectors: known-good frames per RPC, byte-exact; decoder error taxonomy mapped to
  dfmcp-core ErrorCodes with retry classes, each asserted.

title: WP-10 — DFHack mutation bridge: typed prepare/commit/lookup/cancel
description:
## Deliverable
First reversible effects through the bridge: exact pause/resume, then the registered action
families (design/registries/ACTIONS.md: designate dig/channels/stairs, building placement, labor,
work orders, stockpiles, squads, burrows, standing orders).

## Scope
- Typed operation dispatch + operation lookup (LookupOperation RPC) for indeterminate resolution.
- Durable dispatch-attempt journal entries (with WP-11 ledger).
- Game-thread precondition checks at the bridge; short-lived effect tickets (ARCHITECTURE.md
  witnessed mutation sequence).
- Fault-injected reconciliation suite: dropped request/receipt, duplicate, partial batch (TEST-015).
- Crash replay + version certification per action family; each family ships independently
  (ROADMAP Phase 6 order: pause/resume → labor → burrows → stockpiles → work orders).

## Acceptance gate
`fault-injected reconciliation suite` green per family; `GATE-060` exit per family.

## Background
Dispatch success ≠ mutation success ≠ goal success (README). Bridge transport ack is not game
mutation; game mutation is not goal completion. Every mutation: prepare → revalidate → commit →
observe → prove (ADR-006), with compensation where valid (ADR-009).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Per action family: prepare→commit→observe→prove happy path with full receipt logging, then
  the fault matrix: dropped request, dropped receipt, duplicate dispatch, partial batch, game
  crash between journal and effect — expected reconciliation outcome asserted per scenario
  (TEST-015), each scenario emitting a journal excerpt + resolution log.
- Pause/resume certified first (exactness: anchor + pause-state postconditions), then families
  in ROADMAP Phase 6 order.
- Negative evidence: indeterminate outcomes must remain indeterminate — assert no silent retry.

title: WP-12 — Checkpoint/restore: sealed save snapshots and epoch reset
description:
## Deliverable
Production checkpoint/restore to the WP-12 gate.

## Current state
MemoryAdapter checkpoint/restore with epoch invalidation + receipt types; dfmcp-mcp

## Acceptance gate

title: WP-13 gate 3 — MCP Tasks binding backed by the obligation engine
description:
## Task
Make the bounded-obligation engine the application-owned store behind MCP 2026-07-28 Tasks
(`ServerBuilder::final_tasks`), so tasks/get|update|cancel project real dfmcp obligation state.

## Current state
Upstream serves official Tasks methods by default with a process-local in-memory store and
explicitly supports replacing it: "Call ServerBuilder::final_tasks to supply an application-owned
store" (fastmcp_rust README qualification boundaries). dfmcp obligations live in dfmcp-lab
dispatch_step + poll_action with terminal/failure predicates, deadline_tick, poll cadence,
stability requirements (WP-07).

## Deliverables
- TaskStore impl mapping obligation id ↔ MCP task id; state projection:
  working→input_required→completed/failed per MCP task semantics while dfmcp CommitState remains
  authoritative (verified/compensated/cancelled/failed/indeterminate).
- tasks/cancel routes into request/drain/compensate/finalize — never record deletion.
- tasks/get returns evidence references + obligation predicates in task payload.
- Deterministic tests under the lab virtual clock (coordinate WP-07); cancellation at task
  boundaries (TEST-017).

## Acceptance
WP-13 gate 3 closed: long-running fortress operations visible as MCP tasks with honest states;
indeterminate stays indeterminate.

## Background
This is the deepest structural fit of the adoption: MCP Tasks formalize what ADR-007 already
requires (bounded obligations with terminal predicates). See docs/FASTMCP_INTEGRATION.md §5
gate 3 and COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN Part XXII §22.4.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- tasks/get|update|cancel mapped to obligation states under the lab virtual clock; full
  task-state transition logs with obligation predicates and evidence refs in payloads.
- tasks/cancel on a verified task refused; on a running task → drain/compensate/finalize
  sequence asserted (TEST-017 interplay).

title: WP-16 — FrankenSearch attention: evidence-ranked attention and memory
description:
## Deliverable
Progressive attention over fortress state: immutable search/knowledge generations, evidence-ranked
rankings, standing analyses.

## Scope (README attention ranking + docs/FORTRESS_GRAPH_ALGORITHMS.md)
- Attention layer ranks starvation risk, idle critical workshops, blocked jobs, military threats,
  mandate risk, resource bottlenecks, unusual stress, plan regressions.
- Every score carries a ledger of contributing signals + supporting evidence (no unexplained
  rankings; MCP_SURFACE.md fortress.explain consumes these).
- One immutable generation per request; progressive refinement stops on budget while preserving
  completeness status; adaptive policies clamped, sample-gated, circuit-broken (FrankenSearch
  doctrine; architecture/franken_imports.json).
- Deterministic relevance ledger (TESTS.md; WP-16 gate).

## Acceptance gate
`deterministic relevance ledger` green; evidence-backed explain integration with fortress.explain.

## Background
Derived cognition plane can accelerate but never authorize mutation or contradict canonical
evidence (ARCHITECTURE.md plane boundaries).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Deterministic relevance ledger: fixed scenario → fixed ranked output with per-signal
  contribution rows; snapshot-tested (diff log on drift).
- Budget: progressive refinement stop-points asserted; completeness status preserved in results.
- Adaptive policy: clamps + minimum-sample + circuit-breaker tests with policy decision logs.
- Taint: hostile inputs never alter authority (TEST-020 interplay).

title: WP-18 — asupersync production runtime: structured effects/regions/lab
description:
## Deliverable
Move from std scaffolding to asupersync as the exclusive runtime: region-owned work, Cx authority,
deterministic lab.

## Scope
- Every session/plan/bridge op/obligation/checkpoint/graph-search builder/ATP transfer/evidence
  writer is region-owned; region close implies quiescence (project AGENTS.md; ARCHITECTURE.md
  owned execution).
- Every blocking/effectful function receives Cx: authority, deadlines, multidimensional budgets,
  cancellation, replay identity. Cancellation: request/drain/progress certificates/finalize.
- Deterministic Lab integration: virtual scheduler, schedule exploration, fault/crash campaigns
  (IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md lab row; Q2 deterministic campaigns in
  docs/LOCAL_QUALIFICATION_AND_RELEASE.md).
- No second runtime, no detached tasks, no background executors — ever (closed universe).

## Acceptance gate
`cancellation and replay gate` (TEST-017 cancellation: request at every await/effect boundary, no
owned-work leaks; TEST-021 deterministic replay).

## Background
asupersync is sole runtime/structured-concurrency substrate/cancellation model/lab/ATP foundation
(project AGENTS.md). Library surfaces accept caller-owned contexts (fastmcp_rust does the same —
the two stacks share this doctrine).

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Region quiescence: session close with in-flight work → drain or explicit cancellation, never
  orphans (audit log per close).
- Cancellation-at-every-await: systematic injection across effect boundaries (TEST-017) with
  per-boundary outcome logs.
- Replay: identical virtual schedules → identical transcripts across platforms (TEST-021);
  divergence reported at first mismatching anchor/field.
- Runtime audit: CI check that no second runtime enters the graph (already enforced by the
  dependency policy — keep).

title: WP-19 — FrankenFS checkpoint backend: manifests/doctor/repair

title: WP-20 — Operations and packaging: releases, doctor, bundles, support matrix
description:

title: WP-21 — MCP conformance and dogfooding: suite on the pinned revision
description:
## Deliverable
Prove the pinned fastmcp_rust revision against the MCP 2026-07-28 conformance suite through THIS
integration, and run the upstream defect loop end to end.

## Current state (2026-08-29)
- Pin: fastmcp_rust 6481d49 (fixes upstream #59 server gating, #60 transport SseEvent gating).
- Full workspace verify.sh green on Linux nightly at this pin.
- Raw stdio probe confirmed: framing + era negotiation live; modern-era session handshake details
  (server/discover params, per-request _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"] markers,
  initialization-based-MCP-disabled behavior) observed but NOT yet locked into a conformance test.
- Upstream advanced to v0.8.0 preflight (12d3469+) with further restructuring — a pin bump is
  pending (see dfmcp-fastmcp-pin-bump-v080).

## Scope
- Stand up the upstream conformance suite against `dwarf-fortress-mcp serve`; record results in
  docs/DOGFOODING_FASTMCP.md conformance table (TEST-023).
- Lock the modern stdio session shapes into golden tests: server/discover params, tools/list
  params requirements, per-request era marker rules, notification rules (observed:
  MixedInitializeAndModernMetadata rejected; initialize-based MCP disabled in this profile).
- Complete one full defect cycle: find → minimize on the lab → file upstream → upstream fix →
  pin bump → conformance note (TEST-024). #61 (feature-less server build impossible) is the
  first open candidate.
- Pin-bump review for v0.8.0: re-run verify.sh + conformance, update pin-history table.

## Acceptance gate
TEST-023/TEST-024 evidence recorded in docs/DOGFOODING_FASTMCP.md.

## Background
Dogfooding is the point of the modern-only mandate (ADR-013): dfmcp is the hammer that finds
fastmcp_rust spec/gating defects. dfmcp-side workarounds for transport defects are prohibited
unless annotated DOGFOOD-WORKAROUND + upstream link.

## Tests & evidence (in scope)
- Conformance suite run per pin: suite output archived verbatim under
  `docs/DOGFOODING_FASTMCP.md`-referenced artifact dirs, with pass/fail per spec section.
- Golden stdio session tests (from dfmcp-wp13-modern-handshake-golden) run in verify path.
- Defect-loop ledger: every finding → upstream issue URL → fix rev → conformance rerun note
  (TEST-024); workaround-without-link is a lint failure in review.
- Budgets: token/latency envelopes per tool call logged (TEST-022 interplay).
